paragraphs.text: "Jason's here!" Bobby cried.
Jason ran to his friends. It was summertime. Everyone was taking a cooking class together at a farm. Jason couldn't wait to see what they cooked first!
"We're all here now," Nina said.
"Except for Ethan," Izzie said.
"He's having fun surfing in California," Bobby said.
"Well . . ." Jason grinned. "We'll be having fun with a real chef!"
A tall man came over. "My name is Charles. But my students call me Chef. I'll show you junior chefs around the farm. Follow me."
"He seems serious," Nina whispered.
"He's a real chef," Jason said. "So, he is serious—about cooking!"
Several chickens ran around the farmyard.
"Aw!" Izzie saw goats too. "Look at the cute goats in their pen!"
Chef gave the kids baskets. "We're making omelets today," he said. "Let's go to the coop to gather eggs."
At the coop the kids began collecting eggs from nests.
"Be careful not to crack them," Chef said. "We can't use cracked ones. And I don't like to waste food!"
A big dog ran up, wagging her tail.
"This is Cinnamon," Chef said.
"At least the dog is friendly," Bobby whispered.
Finally they went into the farmhouse kitchen.
"It's huge," Jason said.
Chef nodded. "This is my first class for kids. But . . ." He pointed to a poster of kitchen safety rules. "I expect you to follow the same rules that grown-up cooks follow."
"Chef is mean!" Izzie whispered.
"No, he's not," Jason said.
Jason saw a recipe for a cheese omelet on a screen.
"That recipe looks easy!" Bobby said.
Chef frowned. "It's a simple recipe. But making an omelet is not easy. Folding it can be difficult. Let's get started."
The kids washed their hands and put on aprons.
Nina read the instructions. "First we have to crack the eggs."
"I'll crack them!" Bobby said.
"No, no! Not against the bowl!" Chef snapped. "Crack them on a flat surface."
Nina and Bobby carefully cracked two eggs into a bowl. Bobby added salt and black pepper and whisked the mixture a few times.
"Keep whisking!" Chef said.
The eggs were finally ready.
Chef heated a pan on the stove and melted the butter. "We can add the eggs now."
Nina poured in the eggs. They cooked for a few minutes. Then Izzie sprinkled cheese on one side.
"Now we'll fold half of the omelet over the cheese," Chef said.
"Can I do it?" Jason asked. "I know how!"
Chef handed over a spatula. "Be careful."
Jason loosened the omelet's edges. He could feel Chef's eyes on him. When he tried to fold the omelet, his hand shook. It broke apart!
"The omelet is ruined!" Chef sighed. "Let's just eat it and make another one."
Jason hung his head as Chef passed out servings. "Izzie's right," he thought. "Chef is mean."
"Yum!" Nina and Izzie said.
"Best omelet ever!" Bobby said.
Something amazing happened. Chef smiled!
"The omelet doesn't look perfect, but it tastes wonderful. Good job." Chef Charles nodded at Jason.
Chef Jason grinned—and took a taste.
Bobby frowned as he went into the kitchen. He didn't like cooking class so far. Chef was strict, and he had so many rules.
But Bobby's eyes lit up when he saw the recipe. "We're making meatballs!"
"That's right," Chef said. "Nina and Jason, you can start on the meat mixture. Bobby and Izzie, you can prep the other ingredients."
"I wanted to do the meat," Bobby mumbled.
Izzie started chopping a garlic clove.
Chef gave Bobby an onion. "You can chop this."
"That sounds fun," Bobby thought. He quickly got started.
"Bobby!" Chef frowned. "There are rules for using knives. Keep the point of the knife on the cutting board. Then move the knife up and down—like this. The onion needs to be finely chopped."
"Yes, Chef." Bobby didn't know what was wrong with his way. And the onion was making his eyes water. He wiped his eyes.
"Now your hands aren't clean, Bobby!" Izzie said.
"Clean hands are a kitchen rule," Chef said. "Go wash your hands again."
Bobby sighed as he walked to the sink. "More rules."
Soon Bobby and Izzie finished chopping.
Chef was standing by the bowl of meat. "Bring those ingredients over here," he said.
"We already added the egg, bread crumbs, and soy sauce," Jason said.
"Here's the garlic, onion, oregano, and parsley," Izzie said. She dumped everything into the bowl.
Jason and Nina wet their hands. Then they mixed everything together.
Chef wet his hands too and grabbed some of the meat mixture. "Now we'll make the meatballs. Roll it in your hands until you have a small ball."
Everyone started forming meatballs.
Bobby proudly held up his meatball. "Look! Mine is almost as big as a baseball!"
"That's too big!" Chef snapped. "It will take too long to cook. They should be a little smaller than a golf ball."
Bobby sighed and did as he was told.
The kids put their meatballs on an oiled baking sheet.
"We have to wash our hands again," Jason said. "We just handled raw meat."
"That's right," Chef said. He put the meatballs in the oven. "While they cook, please pick some green beans in the garden. Another class will cook them tomorrow."
The kids grabbed baskets and went outside.
"It's nice to be outside," Bobby said. "Chef has too many rules in the kitchen."
"You like sports," Nina said. "Sports have lots of rules."
Izzie nodded. "They make games fair."
"In the kitchen, rules make cooking safe," Jason said.
"I guess." Bobby shrugged.
When the kids went back inside, the timer was going off.
Chef set the baking sheet on the counter. "I made a dipping sauce. It has honey, olive oil, mustard, vinegar, dill, and salt."
"Yum!" Bobby got a meatball and took a bite.
"Ouch! Hot, hot, hot!" he cried.
"Bobby!" Chef said. "Never eat anything right out of the oven. Always let it cool first." He gave Bobby a cool glass of water.
Bobby swished the water around his mouth. "I get it now. Kitchen rules are important!"
Chef greeted the kids in the farmyard. "We're making strawberry shortcake today. Please pick some strawberries in the garden. I'll get things ready inside."
Nina bounced up and down. "I love strawberry shortcake!"
Bobby chuckled. "Of course you do!"
"Hey!" Jason said. "That's a great nickname for you— Short cake!"
Nina glared at him. "Don't call me that."
Bobby and Jason laughed. Izzie frowned at the boys.
The kids picked the strawberries and took them to the kitchen.
"Let's get started," Chef said. "First, we'll wash the strawberries and remove the leaves."
Next, everyone sliced the strawberries. Izzie preheated the oven while Chef greased a square pan. "We need a large mixing bowl. Would someone get one, please?"
"I will!" Nina said. The bowl was on a high shelf. She stood on a stool, but she still couldn't reach it.
"Need some help, Shortcake?" Bobby stretched up and got it.
Nina frowned. "I don't like that nickname!"
Jason was reading the instructions. "We have to mix soft butter and sugar in a large bowl."
Izzie mixed the butter and sugar until it was fluffy. Then she added an egg and vanilla.
"I'll get the dry ingredients ready," Jason said. He mixed flour, salt, and baking powder together.
"Now, mix in half of the dry ingredients and milk," Chef said. "We only do half at a time. This keeps the shortcake from getting too thick."
Jason and Bobby added their ingredients, and Izzie stirred.
"And repeat!" Izzie said.
Jason and Bobby added the rest of the dry ingredients and milk. And Izzie stirred again.
Nina was watching everyone make the batter. "Cooking isn't fun today," she thought.
"Everything is well combined," Chef said. "Nina, please spread the batter in the pan."
"Okay," Nina said softly.
Chef put the pan in the oven. "The shortcake bakes for 25 minutes. Let's make the whipped cream."
"We need heavy whipping cream, sugar, and vanilla," Izzie said.
Bobby whipped everything with a mixer.
"Whipped cream is ready when it forms peaks," Chef said.
He put a whisk in the mixture to check it. When he lifted it, Nina saw peaks in the cream.
Bobby grinned. "It's perfect!"
While the shortcake finished baking, the kids cleaned up. Then they took the food scraps outside.
"The boys keep teasing me today," Nina whispered to Izzie.
"I noticed," Izzie said. "Maybe—"
"Woof!" Cinnamon was pacing near the chicken coop.
"What's wrong, Cinnamon?" Jason asked.
Bobby looked under the coop. "A baby chick is stuck." He reached for it but couldn't get it. He was too big to fit under the coop.
"I'll try." Nina slid under the coop and pulled the tiny chick out.
"Wow!" Bobby said. "Nina saved the day!"
Nina grinned. "Sometimes it's good to be short!"
Back inside, the shortcake was ready. Chef cut it into squares. The kids put strawberries and whipped cream on each serving.
"Mmm. This is yummy!" Nina said.
Bobby patted her back. "Of course it is. We like shortcake."
Jason grinned. "And we like Nina."
Izzie was smiling as everyone put on their aprons. "Something exciting happened yesterday!"
"What?" Nina asked.
"Mom said I was being super responsible taking care of Gurpy. So she let me get a hamster. I named her Nibbles."
"Wow, that's cool!" Jason said.
Chef pointed to the recipe. "Today we're making vegetable pancakes."
Bobby made a face. "Vegetables? In pancakes?"
"Oh, yachaejeon !" Nina said. "They're Korean pancakes."
"That's right," Chef said. "Let's prep the vegetables. We need two and a half cups."
"That's a lot of vegetables," Bobby said.
"Vegetables are good for you!" Izzie said. "Eating healthy food is responsible."
Nina read the ingredients. "Onion, carrot, zucchini." Then she paused. "Um, Chef? Can we use green onions? My aunt uses them when she makes yachaejeon ."
"Sure," Chef said. "We can use any kind of vegetables."
The kids started cutting vegetables into strips. Izzie cut a carrot. Bobby sliced an onion. Jason worked on a zucchini.
Izzie pointed to the recipe. "You're supposed to cut it into thin strips, Jason."
Jason shrugged. "They all taste the same."
"Be responsible and follow the directions," Izzie said. "My carrot slices look perfect."
"Sorry!" Jason said in a teasing voice. "I'm not as perfect as you are."
Bobby giggled. Izzie frowned at him.
"You boys are immature," Izzie said. " Super immature!"
Nina finished slicing green onions. Once all the vegetables were ready, they put them in a bowl.
"Next we add flour, salt, and water," Jason said.
Nina stirred the mixture until the vegetables were all coated. "It's ready."
Chef added cooking oil to a frying pan. When it was hot, he added the vegetable mixture to the pan. "I'll make one big pancake for now. We can share it."
"Are vegetable pancakes good?" Bobby asked.
Nina nodded. "They're really yummy."
Bobby grinned. "I'll try it. Trying new things is super responsible—like Izzie!"
"Why don't you guys make the dipping sauce?" Chef said.
Izzie put soy sauce, vinegar, and red pepper flakes in a bowl. Bobby shook in some sesame seeds.
"Bobby!" Izzie said. "You didn't measure them carefully!"
"It's fine," Bobby said.
Chef slid the pancake out of the pan. He put it on a plate and cut it up.
Izzie gulped. The pancake didn't look like the pancakes she ate at home. What if she didn't like it? Would her friends tease her?
"Hmm, crunchy and delicious!" Bobby said.
"I'm going to make these at home!" Jason said.
Izzie was quiet.
"Try it," Nina whispered. "It's okay if you don't like it."
Izzie took a small bite. Then a bigger one. "I love yachaejeon !" She smiled. "Almost as much as I love my pets!"
Later Chef gave Izzie some chopped zucchini. "It's a good snack for your hamster."
"Thanks!" Izzie said.
As she walked outside with her friends, she cleared her throat. "I'm sorry if I was bossy today."
"You were bossy!" Bobby said.
"But it's okay," Nina said.
Jason nodded. "And saying sorry is super responsible!"
Jason sat in the farmyard playing a video game. Suddenly someone bumped into his arm.
"Ugh!" Jason cried. "You just made me lose!" He turned to see a goat.
Nina laughed. "The goat wants to play a video game too!"
Chef came outside. "The peaches are ripe, so we'll make peach cookies today. Let's pick some first."
The kids followed Chef to the peach trees. They began picking peaches and putting them in baskets.
"I love peaches," Izzie said.
"Me too." Jason climbed a ladder to reach the branches. With his hands full, he started to come down. But a goat was blocking him.
"Move it!" Jason said.
Bobby laughed. "Those goats are troublemakers!"
Nina looked at the baskets. "Do we need all of these peaches for the cookies?"
"No," Chef said. "But I'll sell some at my farmstand tomorrow."
In the kitchen everyone read the cookie recipe.
"Jason and Izzie, please peel and chop the peaches," Chef said. "Bobby, take care of the butter mixture. Nina, you can whisk the dry ingredients."
Everyone got to work.
Bobby mixed brown sugar and white sugar with butter. Then he added the egg, vanilla, and lemon juice. "Ready for the dry ingredients!"
Nina was still whisking the flour, salt, and baking soda. She put in cinnamon and nutmeg. Then she added the mixture to Bobby's bowl.
"Here come the peaches!" Jason stirred everything together.
Chef lined a baking sheet with parchment paper and greased it.
Izzie began dropping tablespoons of dough onto the baking sheet.
"Keep them about five centimeters apart," Chef said. "Otherwise they'll clump together when they bake."
Chef put the baking sheet in the oven.
"Bake for 14 minutes at 175 degrees Celsius," Izzie said.
"Hmm. We do have a lot of peaches," Chef said. "Let's make a few more batches."
While the cookies baked, the kids washed the dishes.
"We made a lot of cookies," Nina said.
"You can take some home," Chef said. "We'll keep the rest here as snacks."
The next day the kids were in the garden. They were picking vegetables to sell at the farmstand.
"My family loved those peach cookies!" Bobby said.
"I'm glad there are so many left over," Izzie said.
Soon the baskets were full of vegetables. The kids carried the baskets back to the farmyard. Chef was bringing out the peaches.
"A customer!" Izzie said, pointing to a car.
"Oh no! We're not ready yet!" Chef looked around in a panic. "Kids, please grab the signs and the cashbox. They're inside." He jogged toward the farmstand.
The kids carried the things to the stand. Then they went back to get the peaches and vegetables.
"Uh-oh!" Nina shouted.
Izzie gasped. "The goats made a mess. And they're eating everything!"
"I knew they were troublemakers!" Bobby said.
Chef groaned. "Now what? We don't have much to sell."
Jason looked at the goats. "I have an idea, but we need a new sign!"
Later the kids closed the farmstand.
Chef turned to Jason. "Selling the leftover peach cookies was a great idea. Everyone loved feeding the goats too! Thank you, Jason."
Jason gave a goat a cucumber. "Glad I could help!"
Bobby was glad to be outside for the start of cooking class. The kids were picking tomatoes to make tomato and pasta soup.
Bobby picked a plump tomato. It felt warm in his hand. He picked two more. That gave him an idea. "Hey, want to see me juggle?"
His friends watched him.
Bobby tossed the tomatoes in the air. He caught one but dropped two.
Jason handed Bobby another tomato. "Here, try it with just two."
Bobby juggled the two tomatoes without dropping them.
"That's pretty good," Nina said.
Jason handed Bobby one more tomato. "Now try three at a time."
"Ugh!" Bobby dropped two. "It’s harder than it looks!" He glanced at the tomatoes on the ground. "Uh-oh."
"What's wrong?" Izzie asked.
Bobby picked up a tomato. "Look, it’s all squishy." The other tomatoes were bruised too.
Nina gulped. "Chef will be mad. He doesn't like to waste food."
"I hope we don't ruin the tomato and pasta soup," Izzie said.
"Maybe he won't notice," Bobby said. "Let's put the bruised tomatoes on the bottom of the basket. We'll put good ones on top."
The kids carried the baskets inside.
"Such beautiful tomatoes!" Chef said. "Our soup will be delicious."
The kids exchanged nervous looks.
"Let's start cooking," Chef said. "First we'll dice one tomato. We'll cut the rest of them into quarters."
The kids began cutting. Soon the good tomatoes were cut up.
Chef picked up a bruised tomato. "What happened? Here’s another bruised one! And another!"
"I—It's . . . my fault," Bobby said. "I tried juggling them, and dropped a bunch. I'm sorry."
Chef frowned.
"Should I throw the bad tomatoes in the compost bin?" Bobby asked.
"Of course not!" Chef said. "We're not wasting these tomatoes. And bruised ones are fine in this soup."
"Phew!" Bobby said.
"Just don't juggle vegetables or fruit again during class," Chef said.
They finished cutting up all the tomatoes.
"Now we have to puree the quartered tomatoes," Izzie said.
They put the tomatoes into a blender. Whirr! Soon the tomatoes were a smooth puree.
Bobby grinned. "No more bruised tomatoes!"
Izzie chopped green onions while Bobby chopped garlic. Nina added olive oil to a large pot. Jason cooked the green onions and garlic in the oil.
Then Chef gave Bobby a mesh strainer. "Hold this over the pot."
Bobby held the strainer while Chef poured the pureed tomatoes through it. Next they added the diced tomato, heavy cream, water, salt, and black pepper.
"Now we add the pasta," Izzie said.
Chef nodded. "It makes the soup rich and filling. You can use any short pasta like farfalle or macaroni."
"I like farfalle. That pasta looks like bowties!" Jason said.
Soon a wonderful aroma filled the air. Ding! The timer went off.
"The soup's ready!" Nina said.
Chef passed out steaming bowls of soup. He sprinkled fresh basil leaves on top.
Bobby tasted the soup. It was warm and delicious.
Chef looked at Bobby. "I hope you learned something today."
Bobby nodded. "I sure did. Tomatoes aren't balls!"
Izzie and her grandmother walked into cooking class together.
"This will be fun, Isabel!" Grandma said.
"Ugh," Izzie thought. "She called me Isabel again!"
Izzie wanted to tell Grandma that she didn't like being called Isabel. But she didn't want to hurt Grandma's feelings.
The boys were washing their hands.
"Hi, Bobby and Jason!" Izzie said. "This is my grandma."
"Hi," the boys said together.
"Our friend Nina isn't here today," Jason said. "Her family is visiting Korea."
"I take a senior cooking class with Chef," Grandma said. "I missed a class, so I'm doing a make-up with you."
"Cool!" Bobby said.
Chef greeted everyone. "Today we're making Rainbow Stir-Fry."
Grandma looked at the recipe on the screen. "Why is it called 'rainbow' stir-fry?"
"Chef says we should eat the rainbow,'" Izzie said. "That means eating lots of colorful fruits and vegetables. They're full of nutrients."
Grandma pinched Izzie's cheeks. "My little granddaughter is so smart!"
"Yikes!" Izzie whispered to the boys. "This is so embarrassing."
"My grandfather treats me like a baby too," Jason whispered. "Last Hanukkah he gave me a huge stuffed animal."
"Grandparents want us to stay little forever," Bobby whispered.
Everyone got busy chopping vegetables. Grandma cut up red cabbage. Jason chopped broccoli, and Bobby cut the bell pepper. Izzie chopped carrots.
Chef heated oil in a wok. "For stir-fries, we don't add all the vegetables at once. We start with those that take longest to cook." He looked at the class. "What should I cook first?"
"Broccoli?" Bobby asked.
"Nope," Chef said.
"I think carrots take longer," Izzie said.
"Yes! Carrots first, then broccoli," Chef said.
"Bell pepper next," Bobby said.
"Then cabbage," Jason said.

Chef nodded. "Bobby, please open that can of baby corn. It cooks quickly, so we'll add it last." He turned to Izzie. "Please get the chicken from the refrigerator. Your grandmother can cut it into thin strips."
Grandma chuckled. "When Isabel was little, she called the refrigerator a foodrater . Isn't that cute?"
"Not again!" Izzie thought as she got the chicken. "Another embarrassing comment!"

While Grandma sliced the chicken, the kids began making the sauce. Izzie chopped ginger. Jason chopped garlic, and Bobby squeezed the lemon. They added those ingredients to vegetable oil, soy sauce, and honey.
"I'm surprised we're making a healthy dish," Grandma said. "I thought we'd make something that kids like. Like hot dogs."
"I love eating healthy foods and trying new things!" Izzie burst out.
Grandma looked surprised. "Really?"
"Yes!" Izzie said.
"This class is the same as my adult classes," Chef said.
"We learn all about food," Bobby said.
"And how to do things ourselves," Izzie said.
Grandma nodded but didn't say anything.

Jason moved the cooked vegetables to a bowl. Izzie helped Chef stir-fry the chicken. When it was cooked, Bobby put the vegetables back in the wok. Grandma added the sauce. All the ingredients simmered together.
Chef served the stir-fry over cooked rice. "Now we can eat!"
"Yum!" Grandma smiled at Izzie. "You're growing up fast, Isabel, er . . . Izzie."
Izzie grinned. "I'm glad you came today, Grandma."
Nina rushed into the farmyard. "I'm back!"
"Yay!" Izzie hugged Nina. "I missed you."
"How was your trip to Korea?" Jason asked.
"Fun!" Nina said. "My cousin Peter took me to beautiful royal palaces. We went to Namsan Tower and walked along Cheonggyecheon Stream. And I ate so many delicious foods."
The kids went inside.
"Speaking of food . . ." Bobby pointed to the recipe screen. "What are bulgogi cheesesteaks?"
"Nina suggested this recipe," Chef said.
"Peter and I ate beef bulgogi in Korea," Nina said. "It reminded me of Philly cheesesteaks from home. So Mom and I made a cheesesteak with bulgogi for him."
Bobby patted his stomach. "Yum! Cheesesteak!"
"First we'll marinate the beef," Chef said. "Later we'll cook it."
Chef got some meat from the freezer. "I froze this for thirty minutes. It will be easier to slice into thin strips." He began slicing the meat.

The kids started making the marinade. Nina chopped garlic, and Bobby and Izzie chopped green onions. Jason mixed together soy sauce, sesame oil, and brown sugar. Nina added grated pear and black pepper.
"We'll put the meat and marinade in this container," Chef said.
Jason stirred the mixture to coat the meat well. Then he sealed the container. "Now it goes into the refrigerator for two hours."
"What's next?" Izzie asked.
"Can I show everyone my photos from Korea?" Nina held up her phone.
"Sure," Chef said. "After that, we'll weed the garden."
"Time to make the cheesesteaks!" Chef said.
"Finally!" Bobby cheered.
Inside, Chef got out two onions. "Let's slice these first. We need thin strips."
"Wah!" Bobby said. "I'll try not to cry!"
Everyone laughed and began slicing. Next Nina put two tablespoons of butter in a pan. Izzie added the olive oil. After the butter melted, Chef put in the onions.
The onions turned soft and golden as Chef cooked them. "Bobby, please get a plate. We're going to remove the onions from the pan. Now we'll cook the meat over high heat."
The meat sizzled as Chef dropped it into the hot pan. Bobby stirred the meat to cook it evenly.
"Now we cut the sandwich rolls," Nina said. She sliced a long roll in half lengthwise. "Don't cut the roll all the way through. It should open like a book."
Everyone carefully sliced their rolls.
Chef topped the meat with the onions. "What's next, Nina?"
"We add cheese and let it melt. Then we put the meat mixture on the rolls!"
At last the cheesesteaks were ready.
"Delicious!" Bobby said.
Nina smiled. But suddenly she felt sad. Her chin trembled.
"Nina! What's wrong?" Izzie asked.
"I miss Peter. I wish Seoul wasn't so far away."
"Let's send him a photo of us eating bulgogi cheesesteaks!" Jason said.
Nina took out her phone and burst out laughing. "I just got a text from Peter. Look at the photo he sent!"
Nina's cousin was eating a bulgogi cheesesteak!
"That's a wonderful thing about food," Chef said. "It brings us together—even when we're far apart."
Nina nodded. "That makes me so happy!"
Jason saw Chef standing near the recipe screen.
"We're having a baking contest today," Chef said.
Jason's eyes lit up. "That sounds fun!"
"What are we baking?" Izzie asked.
Chef pointed to the screen. "A simple brownie recipe with only four ingredients."
"I love chocolate!" Nina said.
Bobby grinned. "I'm going to win this contest!"
Jason frowned. Bobby always wanted to win everything.
"Izzie and Bobby—you'll be Team 1," Chef said. "Jason and Nina will be Team 2. I'll be the judge."
"Our brownies will taste better!" Izzie said.
Bobby gave her a high-five.
Jason kept quiet. He loved cooking, and he wanted to do well.
Chef had two cooking stations ready. The kids took their places. Chef preheated the oven to 180 degrees Celsius.
Jason looked at the bananas, peanut butter, cocoa powder, and chocolate chips. "Amazing! We only need four ingredients to make brownies."
Nina nodded. "First, we mash three bananas in a bowl."
She and Jason took turns mashing them with a fork.
Team 1 did the same thing.
"We're Number 1! We're Number 1!" Bobby chanted.
"Don't worry, Team 2!" Izzie laughed. "We'll share our winning brownies with you."
"Team 1!" Chef frowned. "Mix your brownies and leave Team 2 alone."
"Sorry, Chef," Bobby said.
Izzie scooped peanut butter into a measuring cup. Then she tried to dump it into the bowl. But the peanut butter stuck to the cup.
"Ugh!" she said.
"Izzie didn't use cooking spray," Jason whispered. "Remember when we made peanut butter dog treats? We learned that tip!"
"Right!" Nina said.
She got the cooking spray and sprayed the measuring cup. Jason measured one-half cup of peanut butter. When he dumped it into the bowl, it slid right out.
"Good job!" Nina said.
Jason bowed. "Thank you."
Nina added cocoa powder next.
At Station 1, Bobby dumped in the cocoa powder too fast. A cloud rose up from the bowl. Izzie had some on her chin.
"Watch it, Bobby!" she said.
"Now we mix everything together," Jason said. He saw Chef watching them closely.
Nina started the mixer and blended the ingredients into a thick batter. Jason folded a half cup of chocolate chips into the batter.
Bobby started shouting. "I can do it!"
"You're making a mess!" Izzie pulled the mixer away from Bobby.
Jason was glad Nina was his partner. Nina greased the baking pan. Jason poured the batter.
Chef put the two pans in the oven. "Team 1's brownies are on the left. Team 2's on the right."
The kids were quiet as they cleaned up. When the timer beeped, Chef took the pans out.
Jason's shoulders slumped. "They look exactly the same. How will you pick a winner?"
Chef smiled. "They probably taste the same too. But that's okay because I declare Team 2 the winner. Nina and Jason, you worked very well together."
Jason and Nina grinned at each other. "Yes!"
When the brownies were cool, Chef cut them into squares. Everybody took one.
"Congratulations, Team 2!" Bobby high-fived Jason.
"Great teamwork," Izzie said.
"Great brownies too!" Jason said.
"Please gather some eggs," Chef said. He handed baskets to everyone. "We're making French toast today."
"Yes!" Bobby cried. "I'm wearing my lucky shirt. Whenever I wear it, something good happens. Once I hit a home run with it!"
Nina put three eggs in her basket. "Thanks, chickens!"
Bobby reached down to grab an egg. He heard a loud rip. "Oh, no! I just tore my good luck shirt."
"That's bad luck," Jason said.
"Bobby, your shirt is too small for you," Izzie said. "No wonder it ripped."
Bobby shrugged. "I bet my mom can sew it."
The kids carried the eggs into the kitchen. Everyone looked at the recipe.
"We need four eggs for French toast," Izzie said.
"Remember to crack them properly!" Chef said.
Each kid cracked an egg into a shallow dish. Jason added milk. Then Bobby whisked the mixture.
"Chef, does French toast come from France?" Nina asked.

"No, people first made this dish in ancient Rome," Chef said. "I heard that a man named French made it popular in America. But I'm not sure it's true. Today people all over the world eat fried egg bread."
Bobby grinned. "I want lots of maple syrup on mine!"
"We'll try different toppings today," Chef said.
"Like what?" Jason asked.
Chef pointed to some ingredients on the counter. Bobby saw ketchup, cheese, peanut butter, and yogurt.
"Ugh," Bobby thought. "This isn't my lucky day after all." He didn't want any of those toppings.
Chef melted butter in a frying pan. "Now let's dip a slice of bread in the egg mixture. We're using stale bread because it soaks up the egg nicely."
Izzie dipped a slice of bread in the egg mixture. She turned it over. "There! I coated both sides. It's ready for the frying pan!"
The other kids each took a turn dipping bread slices. Soon four slices were frying in the pan.
After a few minutes, Chef lifted the corner of each bread slice. "They're golden brown. Let's flip them over."
"I'll do it," Jason said.
"I'll help," Nina said.
When the French toast was ready, Chef put it on plates. "Now choose your topping."
Izzie spread yogurt on her slice. "Yum!"
"I'm going to try mine with cheese," Nina said.
"Ketchup sounds weird, but I'll try it," Jason said.
"That's how they eat it in England," Chef said.
Bobby crossed his arms. "I only like French toast with syrup."

"It's cilantro, which is used in Mexican and Asian dishes. These are just four herbs. You'll get to know them better as you cook more."
It was time to make pesto. Nina dumped the basil into the food processor. Izzie peeled two garlic cloves and added those. Jason poured in pine nuts.
Bobby turned on the processor. It whirred as everything mixed together. Chef slowly poured in half a cup of olive oil. He turned off the machine.
"Yum! Smell that basil!"
Jason grated Parmesan cheese and added it to the mixture. Bobby turned on the processor again.
"My favorite color!" Izzie said. "It's bright green and smooth!"
Jason spread pesto on slices of bread. Izzie sliced the tomatoes, and Nina cut up mozzarella cheese. Bobby put the sandwiches together.
Nina took a bite. She loved all the different flavors. "Now I know what basil looks like! The garden fairies can't trick me ever again!"
When the kids arrived for class, Chef was nowhere in sight.
A man greeted them. "Chef is away on a trip. I'm Nick, and I'm teaching class today."
Bobby cheered. "Hooray! No grumpy Chef!"
Jason frowned at Bobby. "That's not nice."
Nick pointed to the screen. "We're making fruit salsa and baked tortilla chips with cinnamon. Who wants to peel and chop the apple?"
Bobby grabbed an apple. "Let's play catch first!"
He tossed the apple to Izzie. Izzie laughed and threw it back.
"Uh, can you chop the apple, please?" Nick said.
"Sure! After we finish our game!" Bobby said.
Jason was peeling and cutting up a kiwi. "You wouldn't do that if Chef was here."
Bobby laughed. "But Chef's not here."
"We should get busy," Izzie said. She stopped playing and began peeling the apple.
Nina was eating raspberries.
"Please save some for the salsa," Nick said.
"I will." Nina smiled shyly and ate another raspberry.
Bobby picked up two strawberries and put one in each ear. "These make good earplugs!"
Izzie made a face. "Yuck! Don't put those in the salsa."
Bobby laughed. "I'll feed them to the goats." He left the kitchen.
Jason put the sliced kiwi into a bowl. Izzie added the apple. Nina dumped in the raspberries.
"Oops," she said. "Sorry I ate so many raspberries!"
"Where's Bobby?" Nick asked.
They all looked out the window. Bobby was playing with the goats.
"I'm going outside too," Izzie said.
"Wait for me!" Nina followed her.
Jason looked at Nick, who seemed unsure what to do. "Shouldn't you make them come inside?"
Nick shrugged. "I'll try." He walked to the door. "Kids? Could you come back? Please?"
Jason was mad that they were ruining class. "You guys cut it out—now!"
His friends froze and stared at him.
"I'm finishing the recipe," Jason said. "You don't have to help. Just show some manners!"
A minute later the three of them were back in the kitchen. They looked embarrassed.
"Sorry, Nick," Bobby said.
"Me too," Izzie and Nina said.

Bobby sliced the strawberries and added them to the fruit bowl. Nina sprinkled white sugar over the fruit. Izzie sprinkled brown sugar. Jason added strawberry preserves and stirred the salsa together.
Nick covered the bowl in plastic wrap. Then he put it into the refrigerator. "Now we'll make the cinnamon chips."

Bobby preheated the oven and put parchment paper on two baking sheets. Nick sliced tortillas into triangles to form chips. He put them on the sheets. Jason sprayed the chips with cooking spray. Bobby made the cinnamon sugar and sprinkled it on the chips. Nina sprayed them again.
Nick put the chips into the oven. The kids cleaned the kitchen. When the chips were ready, Nick set out bowls of fruit salsa. They dipped the cinnamon chips into the salsa.
"Mmm!" Nina said.
"Nick, please don't tell Chef we were misbehaving," Izzie said.
Nick smiled. "Okay."
Bobby looked at Jason. "You won't tell either, will you?"
"I'm not a tattletale," Jason said. "But you sure made me grumpy today!"
Bobby entered the kitchen and smiled at his friends. "Cooking class will be great today!"
"Why?" Izzie asked.
"Bobby, should we tell the others about your guest?" Chef smiled.
"Not yet," Bobby said. "Let's surprise them."

"Sounds good." Chef nodded and pointed to the recipe screen. "We're making oatmeal raisin cookies today. They'll be dessert for the sack lunches we'll pack. Bobby will tell you more about the lunches later."
"Why the big secret?" Jason asked.
Bobby just grinned.
Chef heated the oven to 175 degrees Celsius. "Let's mix the dry ingredients."

Bobby measured the flour and poured it into a bowl. Nina added one teaspoon of baking soda. Izzie put in one teaspoon of cinnamon. Jason poured in a half teaspoon of salt. Bobby mixed the ingredients together.
Next, Izzie measured three-quarters of a cup of brown sugar. She got a spoon and packed it down.
"Pack it firmly," Bobby said.
Izzie rolled her eyes. "I am!"
She dumped the brown sugar into another mixing bowl. Nina poured in half a cup of white sugar. Jason added 14 tablespoons of butter.
"That's a lot of butter," Bobby said. "But I can do the mixing! I know how to get out all the lumps."
He mixed the butter and sugars until the mixture looked creamy.
Izzie added vanilla. Nina cracked two eggs.
"Don't get any shells in there," Bobby snapped.
"I won't!" Nina said.
"Bobby! Stop being so bossy," Jason said.
"I want these cookies to be perfect." Bobby mixed the ingredients again.
"Now add the dry ingredients," Chef said.
"I'll do it!" Bobby said.
"It's Izzie's turn to use the mixer," Chef said.

Bobby frowned, but he stepped aside. Izzie added the dry ingredients to the butter mixture. Then she started mixing. Jason poured in three cups of oats while Nina added raisins. Izzie mixed the dough again.
Everyone took turns dropping spoonfuls of dough onto a baking sheet.
"Nina, yours are too close together," Bobby said. "And Jason's are too small."
Chef sighed. "They're doing fine, Bobby."
Nina put the sheet in the oven.
Chef set the timer for eight minutes. "Time to make the sandwiches," he said.
The kids made tuna salad sandwiches. They put each one in a sack. They added carrot sticks and an apple.
The timer went off.
"Let's check the cookies," Chef said. "They should be golden brown."
The cookies looked perfect. After they had cooled, everyone ate one.
"They're great!" Bobby said, grinning.
The kids put a cookie in each sack.
"Hi, kids!" someone said.
"Grandpa!" Bobby shouted. "The lunches are ready."
"Thank you for making these," Grandpa said.

"The lunches are for older people in our neighborhood," Bobby said. "Grandpa says they sometimes have trouble getting out to shop for food. Some don't have much money, so they might skip meals. I asked Chef if we could help them."
"Great idea!" Nina smiled at Grandpa.
Izzie and Jason nodded.
"Now Grandpa and I will deliver these," Bobby said. "Thanks for helping!"
Nina felt excited. They were helping Chef at the farmstand again. Last time the goats had caused trouble. She hoped things would go smoothly today.
"We're making deviled eggs to sell," Chef said.
"Why are they called deviled ?" Bobby asked.
"A long time ago some spicy foods were called deviled ," Chef said.
Izzie looked nervous.
"Don't worry, Izzie," Chef said. "Our eggs won't be very spicy."
He filled a pot with water and put some eggs inside. He turned on the stovetop. "First, we'll hard-boil the eggs."
After the water started boiling, Chef turned off the stovetop. He put a lid on the pot.
"The eggs will cook in the hot water," he said. "Let's get the farmstand ready."
Chef and the kids set up tables outside.
Nina looked at the goats. "You'd better be good today!"
"I'll keep an eye on them," Jason said.
Fifteen minutes later everyone went back inside. Chef drained water from the pot. The kids carefully plunged the hard-boiled eggs into ice water.
"Cold water stops the eggs from cooking further," Chef said. "It makes them easier to peel too."
The kids went outside to pick vegetables while the eggs cooled.
Nina picked tomatoes. The goats played in their pen. She shook her finger at them. "These vegetables are for customers. Not you!"
"Let's take the vegetables to the farmstand now," Bobby said. "Away from the goats!"
"Yes!" Nina said.
Back inside, Izzie removed the eggs from the water. Everyone dried them and peeled off their shells.
Bobby looked at the recipe screen. "Now we make the filling."

They sliced the eggs in half lengthwise and scooped out the yolks. In a bowl they mashed the yolks with a fork. Jason added mayonnaise. Izzie added yellow mustard. Nina added vinegar and salt and black pepper.
Jason stirred everything together. Then they filled all the egg halves with the yolk mixture.
"Last step," Chef said. "We'll prepare the garnishes."
The kids chopped parsley and green onions, and sliced radishes. They put the garnishes on top of the eggs.
Izzie sprinkled on some paprika. "They look so pretty! Can we try them?"
"Sure," Chef said.
After their snack they were ready for the farmstand. Chef and Izzie carried trays of eggs. Nina held onto the cashbox. Jason and Bobby led two baby goats for the customers to pet.
"Keep them away from the vegetables!" Nina said.
Jason sighed. "I will!"
The farmstand was busy. Nina took money from customers and gave out change. When everything was sold, they walked back to the farmhouse.
Nina led one of the goats. "Hooray! The goats didn't ruin the farmstand today!"
She and Jason put them in their pen.
"How much money did we make?" Chef asked.
Nina gasped. "Oh, no! I forgot the cashbox!"
She and Bobby ran back to the farmstand.
Nina wanted to cry. "If the money is gone, it's my fault!"
But the cashbox was still there with the money inside.
Nina sighed. "The goats were fine. But I almost ruined the farmstand this time!"
It was the last day of cooking class, and Izzie felt nervous. Guests were coming for a special meal after class. She wanted to make Chef proud of them.
"Remember, Chef, don't help us!" Izzie said. "We picked the appetizer recipe ourselves. We can make it ourselves too!"
Chef leaned against the counter. "I won't do a thing. I promise."
"Good," Bobby said.
"Let's get started on the party pinwheels," Nina said. "The cream cheese is soft!"
Izzie put the cream cheese into a bowl. Jason added chopped green onions. Bobby stirred the ingredients together.
They each spread a tortilla with a thin layer of cream cheese.
"Be sure to spread it to the edges," Jason said.
Next they chose fillings. Izzie covered her tortilla with chopped tomato, bell pepper, and cucumber.
Bobby chose ham and cheese. "My pinwheels will be delicious!"
Jason sprinkled diced red onion on his tortilla. He added chicken and avocado.
Nina put sliced mushroom, tomato, and mozzarella cheese on her tortilla.
"Chef will like mine best," Izzie thought. "I used only vegetables from his garden."
The kids rolled their tortillas up to form tubes. They wrapped them in plastic wrap.
"Now we have to chill them. Then they'll be easy to slice," Izzie said. "They have to look like pinwheels!"
They put their rolls in the refrigerator.
Izzie looked at Chef, who was quietly reading recipes. "Good job, Chef."
He gave her a thumbs-up. "You too."
The kids set out everything they had prepared. They had worked hard during the last two classes. There were salmon cakes, cheesy spinach balls, and bread. For dessert, they made peach cookies.
Izzie sighed. "The table looks perfect!"
"Let's finish our pinwheels," Nina said.
They took the tortilla rolls from the refrigerator and unwrapped them. They each sliced their tortilla to create pinwheels.
"They look awesome!" Izzie placed them on two trays.
Just then Cinnamon burst into the room. The dog jumped up, putting her paws on the table. A tray of pinwheels crashed to the floor!
Cinnamon gobbled up several pinwheels before Bobby led her away.
Nina sighed. "At least one tray is left."
"What a disaster." Izzie looked down, waiting for Chef to snap at them.
"I'll help you clean up," he said calmly. "If I'm allowed."
"You must be glad this is our last class," Izzie mumbled.
"What?" Chef shook his head. "I'm so proud of you! You've learned so much—including that cooking sometimes involves mistakes. But there's always a solution."
Izzie smiled. "I'll remember that!"
Soon everything was ready. The first guest arrived.
"Ethan!" the junior chefs shouted happily.
Ethan grinned at them and pointed to the table. "Wow, you made all this?"
"Try a pinwheel," Nina said.
They each took one.
"I'll miss cooking class," Izzie said with a sigh.
"I'm teaching another kids' class during winter break," Chef said.
"Hooray! I'll sign up," Izzie said.
"Can I sign up too?" Ethan asked.
"Of course." Chef nodded. "I've learned something too from this class. Junior chefs are the best!"
